name: Gleniff Barytes Mill
survey: ATU drone lidar (DJI M300 RTK + Zenmuse L1), October 2025, bare earth
notes: Project 1 · The Waters and the Wild

features.name: Mill
features.note: Mill platform · terrace. A level shelf at about +6 m: almost no contours cross it. Cut into the hillside for the mill, with the road along its west side and tight lines on its south side where the ground rises 4–5 m in about 14 m.

features.name: Ballintrillick River
features.note: Valley. Down the west side the contours make Vs pointing south, upstream. The river falls about 8 m as it runs north across the survey.

features.name: Tributary
features.note: Steep valley and gorge. The stream that fed the mill. In the east the lines on both banks nearly touch: a gorge with sides close to 1:2. It drops about 22 m to pass just north of the mill, then runs under the road and on to the river beyond the surveyed area.

features.name: Road
features.note: Made ground. Nature rarely draws straight contours. Where the road climbs south-east across the slope, the contours kink sharply: it sits on a shelf cut into the hillside.

features.name: Bank behind the mill
features.note: Steep bank. Five contours packed into a narrow band: about 1:3. Too steep to walk straight up comfortably; a path would zig-zag.

features.name: Open hillside
features.note: Even slope. North-east of the gorge the lines are evenly spaced, about 4–6 m apart. A steady slope of around 1:12 to 1:16.

splat.source: 3D Gaussian splat (drone photogrammetry), full scan thinned for the web: 1.45 million of 3.69 million splats
splat.note: Aligned to the survey by matching ground under the splat to the bare-earth terrain

geo.note: Survey south-west corner in WGS 84 / UTM zone 29N, matched to the DJI Terra DEM (0.17 m RMS, no rotation). In ITM: E 573946.2, N 849873.2, survey turned -0.81° from ITM grid north.
